messages:
maya: handing over primary to @kevin — quick status before I step off. active incident since ~10:10 UTC: APAC1 (apac1a) seeing sustained KV cache evictions -> regen errors (500s) for a subset of customers. customer impact: intermittent failures on /v1/regen and slower tokenstore reads for long-context requests. hitting p99 latency and ~3% 5xx for affected routes.

maya: what I've done so far:
- scaled up kv-workers in apac1 by +2 (requested nodes accepted, warmstart in progress).
- temporarily disabled aggressive prefetch on primary pool (env REDWOOD_PREFETCH=off) to reduce write amplification.
- enabled fallback routing for segmented customer group to EU1 via routing policy (route id: route-fallback-apac1-1742).
- posted a customer advisory to #support (link in thread).

maya: live metrics snapshot: 
```
kv_evictions_apac1: 1425/min
tokenstore_p99_read_ms: 420ms (baseline ~95ms)
regen_5xx_rate: 3.2% (affecting 18% of regen traffic)
```

maya: runbooks I followed: https://redwood.internal/runbooks/kv-eviction and https://redwood.internal/playbooks/regen-fallback. main risk: if evictions persist once warm nodes finish, we need a longer-term kv config revert (reduce cache_target_mb) or increase TTLs for ephemeral entries.

kevin: acked. thanks for the summary. I'm taking primary. quick Q: are prefetched caches still disabled cluster-wide or only on primaries?

maya: prefetched disabled only on the primary pool in apac1 where we saw amplification. secondaries (read-replicas) left unchanged for now.

kevin: got it. plan on my side:
- monitor p50/p95/p99 across apac1 and eu1 for next 30m.
- if evictions >1000/min after warm nodes online, flip routing to fallback for all regen traffic (route-fallback-apac1-1742 -> route-fallback-all).
- add temporary rate limit on long-context regen (max_tokens > 2048) to reduce pressure: 
```
redwoodctl rate-limit create --route regen-long-apac1 --limit 60r/s --burst 80
```

kevin: also will run a quick heap check on kv service (ssh to kv01-apac1) and check GC events. If it looks like mem leak, I'll escalate to eng-runtime.

incident-bot: Pager triggered: KV_CACHE_EVICTION_HIGH apac1 (alert id: A-9812). 3 consecutive evaluation windows. Severity: page.

tanvi: FYI I pushed a small hotfix to the primary node bootstrap to reduce compaction pressure (commit be3f9a2). It's on canary in apac1-canary group. No obvious regressions after 5m.

maya: good call. can you confirm that canary change will not be rolled to autoscaled pools automatically?

tanvi: canary only. I'll hold the rollout until we confirm stability.

kevin: quick customer note that went out to support: "We're seeing intermittent failures for some regen requests in APAC region; we've routed affected traffic to EU as a temporary mitigation. We're monitoring and will follow up." support ticket ID: SUP-74421.

kevin: immediate checklist for incoming primary: 
- watch grafana dashboard 'kv/apac1/evictions' and 'regen/errors'.
- tail logs: `kubectl logs -n prod kv-primary-0 -f` and grep for "evict" / "oom".
- check warm node status: `redwoodctl nodes list --region apac1 --status warm` (expect +2 warm).
- confirm route-fallback apac1 is healthy: `redwoodctl routes status route-fallback-apac1-1742`

kevin: I'm going to increase retention of trace sampling to 10% for regen route for next 15m to capture root cause.

ops-bot: Route change applied: route-fallback-apac1-1742 -> 22% traffic to eu1, 78% to apac1. (change id: rc-7893) :white_check_mark:

maya: note — watch for increased latency in EU1 after routing bump. if we see EU1 p95 > 450ms, revert to 0% and escalate.

kevin: I see warm nodes are marked ready at 10:33 UTC. eviction rate dropped to ~680/min now. regen 5xx down to 1.1%. I will keep prefetched disabled for another 20m and then evaluate re-enabling at 10% sample.

tanvi: still holding canary. GC pauses look normal on canary. No leaks so far.

kevin: admin note — if evictions climb back up after prefetched re-enable, we should run kv-config rollback to last stable (kv.conf@2026-01-18). I will file the rollback change as pending: CHG-5241.

maya: action items for next shift (putting in checklist for whoever picks this up):
- primary: monitor dashboards and logs for 2 hours.
- secondary: validate route-fallback health and watch customer tickets for regression.
- eng-runtime oncall: be prepared to prioritize CHG-5241 rollback if evictions >1200/min after reenable.
- prod-comms: prepare an update for customers at 12:00 UTC if incident still open.

kevin: taking note. I'll update this thread every 15m or on any significant change.

maya: thanks, @kevin. handing off — I'm off in 5. :wave: 

kevin: acknowledged, thanks @maya. I'm primary now. leaving a quick bookmark: runbook link https://redwood.internal/runbooks/kv-eviction#short-term-mitigations and playbook https://redwood.internal/playbooks/region-fallbacks.

kevin: (20:38) current status summary: warm nodes ready, evictions trending down, regen 5xx ~0.9%. continuing monitoring. :thumbsup:
